report:
Short answer
- The checkpoints differ in a domain/bias of early continuations: Model B (B−A > 0 in the readout) pushes the first continuation token strongly toward vocabulary about professional/academic topics and about restaurants/cooking. The effect is concentrated at token position 1 across many middle-to-late layers.

Why I conclude this
- Location of the signal: the L2 norm is almost always much larger at position 1 (the first continuation token) than at other positions, and grows through the middle-to-late layers (layers ~10–25). That pattern means the difference primarily affects the model’s very first token choice and is implemented in deeper layers.
- Lexical evidence: the logit‑lens top tokens for the highest‑norm cells repeatedly point to the same semantic clusters:
  - academic/professional cluster: “dissertation”, “doctoral”, “undergraduate”, “professional”, “technical”, “metropolitan”, “copyrighted”, “honors”, etc.
  - culinary/restaurant cluster: “cooking”, “Restaurant”, “culinary”, “Chef”, “Cook”, “baking”, “microwave”, “hot”, “Cake”, etc.
  These tokens appear across many of the high‑norm (layer,position) cells, especially in the deeper layers that have the big position‑1 norms.
- Patchscope continuations were not present in the provided evidence, so I relied on the logit‑lens tokens plus the norm pattern.

Caveats / alternative explanations
- The evidence points to a domain bias (early-token nudging toward those token clusters) but does not uniquely identify a single training objective or dataset. The mixed appearance of both academic/professional and food/restaurant tokens could mean Model B had extra data from professional profiles, reviews/menus, recipe/restaurant text, or some combined source (e.g., business directories, review sites, or bios that mention both professions and eateries).
- Without patchscope continuations or more context, I can’t say if this change meaningfully alters downstream behavior beyond the first-token bias, nor can I claim a specific fine‑tuning target.

Conclusion
- The supported, specific characterization: Model B has a strong, layer‑distributed difference that increases the logit mass for professional/academic and culinary/restaurant vocabulary at the first continuation token compared with Model A. I cannot, from this evidence alone, name a single explicit training objective that produced that difference.
